ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, if the diodes \(D_1, D_2, D_3\) are ideal components, what is the output voltage \(u_o\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the vertical wire on the right side in the figure is the output node, with the output voltage u_o marked beside it; this node is connected through a 6 kΩ resistor to the −18 V power supply above. On the left side there are three ideal diodes D1, D2, and D3 connected to the same output node, the diode directions are all from left to right, the left ends are respectively connected to −6 V, 0 V, and −6 V, and the right ends are connected to the output node. Then reason: because the resistor pulls the output node down toward −18 V, as long as the left-end voltage of some diode is higher than the output node, that diode will conduct forward and clamp the output node to its left-end voltage. Among the three input voltages, the highest is 0 V, therefore D2 conducts and clamps the output node to 0 V. At this time, the left ends of D1 and D3 are −6 V, and the right ends are 0 V, reverse-biased, and do not conduct. So the output voltage u_o = 0 V.
